This theater performance tells, with humor and tenderness, the chaos of moving as seen by a somewhat lost dad, surrounded by cardboard boxes and childhood memories.

PAPA is moving house. He’s completely lost! He can’t find anything anymore, not even his... child! Cardboard boxes everywhere – what an incredible playground! 

When you move, you leave something behind… or someone… 

And you realise there’s a piece of paper missing from the child’s every drawing hanging on the wall… 

When you move house, everything is upside down! You no longer know which way is up or down. You don’t know if everything that’s happening is real or if you’re in a funny dream. 

In a playful and humorous way, the actor shows curious minds how masks and puppets can be made from pieces of packaging cardboard using simple and inexpensive methods.

OLEMA is a contemporary circus performance exploring and attuning itself to the experience of connection and the undoing of anthropocentrism.

The piece takes its inspiration from the story of an extinct bird, whose solitary song ends in silence. On the stage, acrobatics, dance, music and visual art meld together. The performance asks, what is left after a loss, and if what has been lost can still be found in the body, voice, and movement. 

** 

Circus offers a singular context for this inquiry: its history is entwined with the thresholds between the human and the more-than-human – from the serpent-like contortionists (käärmeihminen, ‘snake-human’ in Finnish), to beast tamers, and legacies of bodily dehumanisation. 

The dramaturgical core of the work grows from the extinction story of the Kauaʻi ʻōʻō bird species. The last male of the species continued to sing its duet-form mating call even after the last female had disappeared in a hurricane in 1982. Space tourism promises new opportunities—but at what cost? Is travelling to space true progress, or an escape from the problems we have left unresolved on Earth

Transport: Fasten your Seatbelts! is a dazzling, ironic satire that invites us to look at a fractured world from a distance—from above—where its contradictions become sharper and harder to ignore.

At the center of the story is Megan, an ambitious young woman raised to believe that anything is possible if you want it badly enough. 

When she receives the most prestigious birthday gift imaginable—a luxurious trip to space—it seems her dreams have finally come true.

But the view from space reveals another side of the story: beneath the shiny surface of technological progress lies the growing social inequality, environmental exhaustion, and a blind faith in escape as a solution. 

Fasten Your Seatbelts! raises pressing questions about the future of luxury space tourism— offering new horizons while simultaneously exposing deep-rooted inequality and environmental consequences.

Czech Divadlo Alfa's Transport: Tipping Point is a gripping, documentary-style theatre performance that places the audience at the heart of a courtroom drama. 

On the defendant’s bench sits a representative of one of the world’s largest energy corporations, accused of being complicit in one of the most devastating environmental disasters of our time. 

The explosion on the oil rig lays bare the fragility of our systems, the unchecked power of fossil fuel giants, and the lethal entanglement of greed with systemic negligence. 

But the performance is more than a recounting of the largest environmental catastrophe in the U.S.—it is a reflection on a world where nature struggles to survive under the relentless logic of capital. 

Through a striking combination of documentary material, audiovisual storytelling, and live performance, Transport: Tipping Point sparks a dialogue about global transport, human needs, trade, fossil fuels, corporate interests, and the environment. 

It challenges audiences to confront their own responsibility and inspires reflection on the steps we can take toward sustainable living and a more conscious relationship with the natural world.

Tsekkiläisen Divadlo Alfan Transport: Tipping Point on mukaansatempaava, dokumentaarinen teatteriesitys, joka sijoittaa katsojan keskelle oikeussalidraamaa. 

Syytetyn penkillä istuu edustaja yhdestä maailman suurimmista energiayhtiöistä, jota syytetään osallisuudesta yhteen tuhoisimmista ympäristökatastrofeista. 

Öljynporauslautan räjähdys paljastaa järjestelmiemme haurauden, fossiilisten polttoaineyhtiöiden valvomattoman vallan sekä ahneuden ja rakenteellisen välinpitämättömyyden kohtalokkaan kietoutumisen.

Esitys ei kuitenkaan ole pelkkä kertomus Yhdysvaltojen suurimmasta ympäristökatastrofista – se on myös pohdinta maailmasta, jossa luonto kamppailee selviytyäkseen pääoman armottoman logiikan puristuksessa. 

Dokumentaarisen materiaalin, audiovisuaalisen kerronnan ja live-esiintymisen vaikuttavan yhdistelmän kautta Transport: Tipping Point herättää keskustelua globaalista liikenteestä, ihmisten tarpeista, kaupasta, fossiilisista polttoaineista, yritysintresseistä ja ympäristöstä. 

Se haastaa katsojat kohtaamaan oman vastuunsa ja kannustaa pohtimaan, millaisin askelin voi edetä kohti kestävämpää elämäntapaa ja tietoisempaa suhdetta luontoon.

d:
Egotrippi celebrates one of the most significant albums of their career, Vielä koittaa uusi aika , with a special 20th-anniversary concert at Huvila. Released in February 2006, the album became the band’s first to top the Finnish charts, reaching gold status within its first week. 

The concert evening at Huvila in August is divided into two parts: the first half features rare gems from the band’s 33-year career, and the second half features a complete performance of the album Vielä koittaa uusi aika . 

Live on stage, Egotrippi is a warm, melodic, and effortlessly cohesive group whose songs—filled with longing, comfort, and bright choruses—create unforgettable nights with the audience. The band’s signature sound, strong storytelling, and anthemic climaxes make their shows feel simultaneously intimate and grand.

Tailored specifically for Huvila, this anniversary concert offers a rare chance to revisit the album’s timeless landscapes and world of memories, presenting a setlist that will likely never be heard exactly like this again.
